source: async function foo() { throw await bar; }

findings.message: This throws something that cannot be an Error, so whatever catches it gets no message and no stack trace. The failure then surfaces as a bare string or object with no record of where it came from, which is the difference between reading one line and reading the whole call path. Throw `new Error(...)` instead.

source:
declare const foo: unknown;
throw new Error() ?? 'literal';

declare let foo: unknown;
throw foo ??= 'literal';

findings.message: This throws `undefined`, which reaches the handler carrying nothing at all: no message, no stack, no type. It is almost always an expression that was meant to produce an error and did not. Throw `new Error(...)` instead.
